answer: Sequential proof-of-delay prices identity in unparallelizable time. Before a key's vote counts, it must produce a verifiable delay proof, and like a sonnet whose form forbids shortcuts, that computation runs strictly one step at a time: no cluster of machines finishes it faster. Every clone is an island burning its own wall-clock, and the relic each proof leaves behind cannot be shared. A fleet operator gains no parallel speedup, so scale buys nothing - each forged key pays full hardware and delay for one account's slice of reward, and the marginal clone always costs more than it earns.
